chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz narrated from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
A disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim, and a Muslim may inherit from a disbeliever, unless the Muslim has bequeathed something to the disbeliever in a will.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest; he left a will assigning something
key_terms.الْكَافِرُ: a disbeliever; the non-Muslim party in the inheritance ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُ: a Muslim; the believing party in the inheritance ruling
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ: something; a specified portion or item left by bequest
key_terms.يَرِثَ: to inherit; to receive property through inheritance

ai.seo_question: Can a non-Muslim inherit from a Muslim, and can a Muslim inherit from a non-Muslim in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling on inheritance between people of different religions. It establishes that a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim, while a Muslim may inherit from a disbeliever, with mention of a bequest made by the Muslim to the disbeliever.
